body:
If you go once every 3 or 4 days no matter how much water you drink or how much fiber you choke down — and you keep getting told to "just give it time" — I want to tell you what finally made sense of all of it for me.

Because I watched my best friend live it. And once I understood what was actually going on, I'll be honest: I was angry. Not at any one person. Angry that the answer was this simple, and it took us almost two years to find it.

Let me tell you about Gail.

For the better part of two years, my best friend was miserable. Her constipation got so bad she'd go once every five or six days — not "a little backed up," but sitting in the bathroom for 45 minutes, straining, near tears, feeling like her body had simply stopped working.

title: Going Every 3–4 Days No Matter How Much Water You Drink?

body:
Last March I found Wegovy® in my sister's bathroom cabinet.

I closed the door the way you'd close it if you'd just opened a letter that wasn't addressed to you. Quiet. Careful. Like I needed time to decide what I'd just seen.

Seeing a weight-loss drug behind her cotton pads felt like being lied to. A small confounding betrayal I'd needed her to be above.

I didn't speak to her for six months.

I'm on the same drug now.

And there's something I need to tell her before the symptom she's been hiding from me gets worse. I think it's already worse.

Let me back up.

My sister is forty-eight. I'm fifty-nine. We've been close in the way only sisters who survived the same childhood can be close. Three kids between us. One divorce survived (mine). Twenty-six years of Sunday dinners at our mother's table before our mother passed in 2022, and another three years of holding the family together at
title: I Lost My Sister Over Her Wegovy®.
